mainTopic: The impurity status of the פרה אדומה's ash tube, and the source for a כלי joining its contents for קודש
overview: The גמרא first tries to define what kind of impurity the חכמים gave the tube that holds the ashes of the פרה אדומה. It tests three models: an item touched by a שרץ, an item touched by a מת, and an item touched by a מת that is already on its seventh day. A ברייתא about the person who cuts and immerses the tube rules out the first two models. A second ברייתא says the חכמים never made anything new for the פרה. אביי explains that this only means they never made a non-seat, like a spade, count as a מושב, and he brings the source for that rule from a פסוק. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's rule that a כלי joins its contents for קודש but not for תרומה. רבי חנין learns this from the פסוק about 'one pan full of קטורת.' רב כהנא objects that רבי עקיבא's ruling on this same rule is only rabbinic, and he proves it from the ruling about אפר חטאת. ריש לקיש begins an answer in the name of בר קפרא, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The tube is treated like something touched by a creeping animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the חכמים gave the tube the status of an item made impure by a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: They treated it as though it had been made impure by a creeping animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first model for the tube's impurity: it counts as an item that touched a שרץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An item that touched a שרץ is a ראשון לטומאה, a fairly mild level of impurity. This choice fits the earlier discussion about showing opposition to the צדוקים. It also sets up the problem in the next step, because a ראשון לטומאה cannot make a person impure.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the חכמים) made it, meaning they treated it as
Something made impure by touching a dead creeping animal
The hollow reed tube used for the ashes of the פרה אדומה

phrases.english: They treated it as one made impure by a creeping animal.
phrases.notes: "It" is the reed tube used for the פרה ash, which the גמרא has been discussing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer that began on the earlier part of the daf about the tube's impurity.
steps.terutzMaskana: The tube has the status of an item that touched a שרץ.

steps.title: Then it should not make a person impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the שרץ model. A ברייתא says the person who handles the tube needs טבילה, which shows the tube does make people impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, it should not make a person impure. Why then is it taught in a ברייתא: one who cuts it and immerses it needs immersion himself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first model using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An item touched by a שרץ is a ראשון לטומאה, and a ראשון cannot pass impurity on to a person. Yet the ברייתא says the person who cuts and immerses the tube must immerse himself. So the tube must carry a stronger impurity than the שרץ model allows.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, now (introduces the problem that follows from your claim)
Why then?
He cuts it and immerses it
Requires immersion

steps.confusionAlert: "טָעוּן טְבִילָה" is talking about the PERSON who handled the tube, not the tube itself. That is why it proves the tube can make a person impure.

phrases.english: But if that is so,
it should not make a person impure,
why then is it taught in a ברייתא:
One who cuts it and immerses it requires immersion!
phrases.notes: The one who "requires immersion" is the person doing the cutting, so the tube must have made him impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the שרץ model from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the tube is like a טמא שרץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טמא שרץ cannot make a person impure, but the ברייתא shows the tube does.

steps.title: Rather, the tube is treated like something touched by a corpse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא switches models. The tube is treated as an item made impure by a מת, which can make a person impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they treated it as one made impure by a corpse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the שרץ model and suggests a stronger one: the tube is like an item that touched a מת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An item that touched a מת carries strong impurity that can pass to a person. That explains why the ברייתא requires the handler to immerse. The change fixes the problem from step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather (replacing the previous answer)
Something made impure by contact with a corpse

phrases.english: But rather: they treated it as one made impure by a corpse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected שרץ model with a מת model.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifies the impurity at a higher level
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The tube was like a טמא שרץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: The tube is like a טמא מת, so it can make a person impure.

steps.title: Then it should need sprinkling on the third and seventh days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the מת model. Anything impure from a מת needs הזאה on days three and seven, but the ברייתא mentions only immersion.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should need sprinkling on the third and seventh days. Why then is it taught: one who cuts it and immerses it needs immersion? Immersion, yes; sprinkling on the third and seventh days, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second model by reading the same ברייתא closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anything made impure by a מת becomes pure only after הזאה with פרה water on the third and seventh days, plus טבילה. The ברייתא mentions only טבילה, so it implies no sprinkling is needed. That does not fit a full טמא מת status.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
It should require
Sprinkling of the פרה water on the third and seventh days
Yes ... no (this is needed, that is not)

phrases.english: If so,
it should require sprinkling on the third and seventh days,
why then is it taught:
One who cuts it and immerses it requires immersion.

phrases.aramaic: טְבִילָה אִין, הַזָּאַת שְׁלִישִׁי וּשְׁבִיעִי לָא!
phrases.english: Immersion, yes; sprinkling on the third and seventh days, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי תִּיבְעֵי הַזָּאַת שְׁלִישִׁי וּשְׁבִיעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the מת model from step 3, using the same ברייתא as step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the tube is like a טמא מת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full טמא מת needs sprinkling on days three and seven, but the ברייתא implies only immersion is needed.

steps.title: Like a corpse-impure item already on its seventh day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא refines the model. The tube is like a טמא מת that has already reached its seventh day, so it still makes people impure but only needs immersion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they treated it as one made impure by a corpse, on its seventh day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adjusts the מת model so it fits both parts of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא מת on its seventh day has finished its sprinklings but is still impure until it immerses. So it can still make a person impure (answering step 2), and it needs only טבילה (answering step 4). This middle position fits everything the ברייתא says.

keyTerms.meaning: On its seventh day (of the purification process)

steps.whatToRemember: After two failed models, the גמרא settles on: the tube is like a טמא מת on its seventh day. It still passes impurity to people, but it needs only טבילה and no more sprinkling.

phrases.english: Rather: they treated it as one made impure by a corpse
on its seventh day,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: עֲשָׂאוּהָ כִּטְמֵא מֵת בִּשְׁבִיעִי שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refines the step 3 model to answer the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the category to a specific stage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A full טמא מת, which would need sprinkling.
steps.terutzMaskana: A טמא מת on its seventh day, which makes people impure but needs only immersion.

steps.title: But the חכמים never invented new rules for the פרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new answer with a ברייתא saying the חכמים never created anything new in the rules of the פרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: they never made any innovation regarding the פרה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to rule out the last answer. אביי answers this in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the חכמים never created brand-new rules for the פרה that don't exist anywhere else. Treating a tube as if it touched a מת when it never did looks like exactly that kind of new rule. So the step 5 model now seems to break this principle.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? (introduces a challenge)
They did not invent anything new
The פרה אדומה and its purification process

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: מֵעוֹלָם לֹא חִידְּשׁוּ דָּבָר בַּפָּרָה.
phrases.english: But isn't it taught: They never made any innovation regarding the heifer.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא means the חכמים added strictness to the פרה but never invented rules that don't exist anywhere else.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: מֵעוֹלָם לֹא חִידְּשׁוּ דָּבָר בַּפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the refined model from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the tube is treated like a טמא מת on its seventh day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Giving corpse impurity to something that never touched a מת is a new rule, and the ברייתא says the חכמים never made new rules for the פרה.

steps.title: אביי explains what 'no new rules' really means
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the ברייתא only means the חכמים did not rule that a spade becomes impure as a seat (מושב).
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The statement that they made nothing new means only that they did not say a spade becomes impure as a seat.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge from step 6. He narrows the ברייתא: it does not ban every extra stringency, only one specific kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 asked how the חכמים could treat the tube like a טמא מת if they never added anything to the פרה. אביי replies that the 'nothing new' rule only means they never turned an object that is not used for sitting, like a spade, into a מושב. Other stringencies, like the one about the tube, are still possible.

keyTerms.meaning: A spade or axe, a work tool
A seat. When a זב sits on it, it becomes a strong source of טומאה
Becomes impure as a seat of a זב

phrases.english: Abaye said:
[It means] that they did not say a spade becomes impure as a seat.
phrases.notes: He is explaining the ברייתא from step 6. The 'nothing new' rule is limited to this one case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי שלא אמרו קורדום מטמא מושב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by narrowing what the ברייתא means.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the challenging source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say the חכמים added no stringency at all to the פרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only means they did not make a non-seat, like a spade, count as a מושב. Other stringencies are allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the model from step 5, that the tube is treated like a טמא מת on its seventh day.

steps.title: אביי's source: only an object meant for sitting becomes a seat
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that an upside-down measuring bowl that a זב sat on is not a מושב, because it is not meant for sitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'And he who sits on the object.' You might think that if a זב turned over a סאה or a תרקב measure and sat on it, it would be impure. So the פסוק says: 'And he who sits on the object on which he sits... shall be impure.' This means something set aside for sitting. That excludes this kind of object, where we would tell him: Get up so we can do our work.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a ברייתא to show where the rule about 'not a seat' comes from in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the words 'on which he sits' as limiting the law to objects that are normally used for sitting. A tool or measure used for work does not count, since people would ask you to get off it. This is the basic rule that, according to אביי, the חכמים did not make stricter for the פרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A large measuring container
A smaller measuring container
Turned upside down
Set aside for sitting
The פסוק teaches

phrases.english: As it is taught: "And he who sits on the object."
One might think: if [a זב] turned over a se'a measure and sat on it,
or a tarkav measure and sat on it —
it should be impure [as a seat],
so the verse teaches:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְהַיּוֹשֵׁב עַל הַכְּלִי אֲשֶׁר יֵשֵׁב עָלָיו ... יִטְמָא״ —
phrases.english: "And he who sits on the object on which he sits ... shall be impure" —
something that is set aside for sitting;
this is excluded,
since we say to him: Get up, so we can do our work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule אביי mentioned in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The basic rule that a work tool is not a מושב for a זב
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ויקרא 15:6, 'on which he sits'
steps.whatToRemember: The 'nothing new' rule for the פרה only means a non-seat (like a spade) was never made into a מושב. The tube rule from step 5 still stands.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a vessel combines its contents for sacred food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, that a כלי combines its contents for קודש but not for תרומה, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כלי combines what is inside it for קודש, but not for תרומה. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה and sets up the next step by asking for its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that separate pieces inside one כלי count as one unit for קודש. So if טומאה touches one piece, all of it becomes impure. This is stricter than תרומה, so the גמרא wants to know where this extra strictness comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Joins together, making separate pieces count as one
Sacred food, such as קרבנות
The portion of produce given to a כהן
From where are these words? A request for a source

phrases.english: A vessel combines what is inside it for sacred food,
but not for terumah.
From where are these matters [derived]?

steps.triggerLanguage: הכלי מצרף מה שבתוכו לקדש אבל לא לתרומה מנא הני מילי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the פרה and opens a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that a כלי combines its contents for קודש.

steps.title: רבי חנין: the pan full of קטורת counts as one
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנין learns it from the פסוק 'one pan... full of קטורת', which treats everything in the pan as one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנין said: The פסוק says, 'One pan of ten gold shekels, full of קטורת.' The פסוק treats everything in the pan as one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנין answers the question from step 9 with a פסוק about the gifts of the נשיאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the pan 'one' even though it holds many separate grains of קטורת. From this, רבי חנין learns that a כלי makes everything inside it count as one unit for קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: A pan or ladle
Incense burned in the בית המקדש
For the פסוק says

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanin said,
for the verse says:
"One pan of ten [shekels], gold,
full of incense,"

phrases.aramaic: הַכָּתוּב עֲשָׂאוֹ לְכׇל מַה שֶּׁבַּכַּף — אַחַת.
phrases.english: the verse made everything that is in the pan into one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי חנין דאמר קרא כף אחת עשרה זהב מלאה קטרת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק calls a pan full of קטורת 'one', so a כלי unites its contents for קודש.

steps.title: רב כהנא: but רבי עקיבא 'added' this rule
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא objects with a teaching that רבי עקיבא added flour, incense, frankincense, and coals to the rule that a טבול יום who touches part disqualifies all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא objected: רבי עקיבא added fine flour, incense, frankincense, and coals, so that if a טבול יום touched part of it, he disqualified all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא starts a challenge to רבי חנין's source by quoting רבי עקיבא's ruling about a כלי joining sacred contents. The point of the challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנין's פסוק makes it sound like a Torah law that a כלי joins its contents for קודש. רב כהנא quotes רבי עקיבא's ruling, which uses this same joining rule for flour, incense, frankincense and coals. The next two steps show that this ruling is only דרבנן, which clashes with a Torah source.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection from a source
Added
Someone who went to the מקוה today but must wait until nightfall to be fully טהור
Fine flour
Frankincense

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב כהנא is arguing about the law itself. He is questioning whether the joining rule is Torah law. The punchline comes in Step 12: רבי עקיבא's ruling is only rabbinic.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana raised an objection:
Rabbi Akiva added
the fine flour, the incense, the frankincense, and the coals,
that if a tevul yom touched part of it —
he disqualified all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מתיב רב כהנא הוסיף רבי עקיבא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source given in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנין's claim that the joining rule for קודש comes from a פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא's joining rule is rabbinic, as Steps 12-13 show. That does not fit רבי חנין's claim that the joining rule for קודש comes from a Torah פסוק.

steps.title: But that teaching is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא sharpens his challenge: the teaching of רבי עקיבא he just quoted is a rabbinic law, not a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this rule is only rabbinic!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the point of רב כהנא's challenge. The rule he quoted from רבי עקיבא is only rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנין learned from a פסוק that a כלי joins its contents together, which makes it sound like a Torah law. But רבי עקיבא's teaching, which uses the same idea of 'touching part disqualifies all', is only דרבנן. So how can this idea come from a פסוק?

keyTerms.meaning: But this (opens a challenge)
From the Rabbis, a rabbinic law (not from the Torah)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is the punchline of רב כהנא's challenge from Step 11. The teaching he quoted proves the rule is rabbinic, which clashes with רבי חנין's פסוק.

phrases.english: But this is rabbinic!
phrases.notes: 'This' means the rule רבי עקיבא added in Step 11, about a טבול יום who touches part of the contents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection that רב כהנא began in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנין's derivation from the פסוק 'one pan full of קטורת' (Step 10).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule of a כלי joining its contents shows up in a teaching that is only rabbinic. So it cannot be learned from a Torah פסוק.

steps.title: Proof that רבי עקיבא's addition is rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the teaching is rabbinic from the first part of that same משנה. That part is about אפר חטאת, and רבי עקיבא's rule is 'added' onto it.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know it is rabbinic? The first part of that משנה says: רבי שמעון בן בתירא testified about אפר חטאת that if a טמא touched part of it, all of it becomes טמא. Then it says: רבי עקיבא added.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know the teaching is rabbinic. It answers by pointing to the line that comes just before רבי עקיבא's addition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אפר חטאת, the ashes of the פרה אדומה, is not food and not a קרבן. So רבי חנין's פסוק about קטורת cannot apply to it, and that ruling must be rabbinic. Since רבי עקיבא 'added' to that ruling, his addition is the same kind of rule, meaning it is also rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do we know?
The first part of a teaching
He testified, he passed on a ruling
The ashes of the פרה אדומה, used for purifying
Part of it
He added

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא method. You can learn what kind of law a statement is from the statement it is attached to. The word 'added' links רבי עקיבא's rule to the rabbinic rule about אפר חטאת.

phrases.english: From where? From the fact that it teaches in the first part:
Rabbi Shimon ben Beteira testified
about ashes of purification
that if an impure one touched part of it,
phrases.notes: The ashes are sitting inside a כלי, which is why touching one part could affect the rest.

phrases.english: it made all of it impure.
And it teaches: Rabbi Akiva added!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the claim of Step 12 that רבי עקיבא's teaching is rabbinic.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי עקיבא's rule (a כלי joining flour, incense, frankincense and coals) is rabbinic.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first part of the same משנה: רבי שמעון בן בתירא's ruling about אפר חטאת. That ruling must be rabbinic, and רבי עקיבא 'added' to it.

steps.title: ריש לקיש begins an answer in the name of בר קפרא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces ריש לקיש, quoting בר קפרא, who will respond to רב כהנא's challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of בר קפרא:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. It introduces who will answer רב כהנא's challenge, and the actual answer comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge says רבי עקיבא's rule is rabbinic, while רבי חנין says the rule of a כלי comes from a Torah פסוק. ריש לקיש is about to explain how these two fit together. So far we only know who is speaking.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא from ארץ ישראל, also called רבי שמעון בן לקיש
In the name of
A sage from the time of the last תנאים

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said in the name of Bar Kappara:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the response to the challenge raised in Steps 11-13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Not yet stated. This is only the introduction to the answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's rule being rabbinic seems to contradict רבי חנין's Torah source.
steps.terutzMaskana: Still to come. This line only names who gives the answer.
